Zoox is an autonomous ridehailing company building the world's first purpose-built robotaxi — fully electric, bidirectional, with no steering wheel or driver's seat. We're currently operating in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with Austin and Miami on the horizon, and testing underway across seven U.S. markets.

Zoox's part-time student worker program puts you at the center of one of the most ambitious challenges in transportation. You'll contribute to real projects, work alongside engineers and researchers pushing the boundaries of autonomous technology, and gain experience that goes well beyond the classroom. We're looking for students who bring strong academic foundations, curiosity that doesn't stop at coursework, and a drive to be part of something that matters.
Role Overview
This role focuses on building a data-driven safety risk model that quantifies and improves autonomous-vehicle driving performance, along with the data analysis work that supports it. The student will work within the Safety Strategy & Operations team on a 6-month project spanning model development, empirical experimentation, and large-scale driving/simulation data analysis.

Support designing, building, and iterating on a data-driven safety risk model that quantifies driving performance and surfaces safety-relevant signals across the autonomy stack
Assist developing and maintaining dataset management pipelines — curation, labeling, versioning, and quality checks — that feed the risk model and downstream analyses
Support defining and running empirical experiments that “show it with data” rather than relying on assumptions
Required Qualifications
Assist analyzing large-scale driving and simulation datasets to identify trends, edge cases, and opportunities to improve autonomy performance
Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in a relevant quantitative field (Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Physics, or similar)
Strong programming skills in Python
Help work through ambiguous, open-ended problems with a researcher’s mindset and a bias toward rapid iteration
Solid data manipulation understanding (e.g., SQL, PySpark, Scala)
Solid foundation in statistics, machine learning, and risk or reliability modeling
Help communicate complex results, trade-offs, and uncertainty clearly to the team and stakeholders
Comfort operating independently under high uncertainty on open-ended problems

Excellent written and verbal communication; able to convey complexity and ambiguity clearly
Experience with safety, reliability, or risk modeling (e.g., survival analysis, Bayesian methods, causal inference)
Experience with large-scale dataset management, data pipelines, or MLOps tooling

Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, or a related quantitative discipline
Prior research experience taking ambiguous, end-to-end problems from zero to a result, independently

Genuine interest in autonomous vehicles and Zoox’s mission
Currently enrolled in a B.S. or M.S. program in a relevant discipline.
Available to commit to a minimum three-month assignment.

Work hard. Have fun. Make history.

Successful candidates are natural self-starters who have prior engineering experience in the integrated automation project life cycle, including design, development, implementation, enhancement, and support.
System Development Engineers (SysDE’s) will be part of a new product/technology deployment cycle and responsible for successful delivery of equipment for further testing and evaluation. You will serve as a liaison between Fulfillment Center Operations (our customer) and product development engineers.
This role will require the ability to build relationships across a cross-functional team and capture and synthesize the voice of the customer. Your primary goal is to own the improvement of the deployment process, validating and testing processes through lab and field activities. You will integrate, deploy, and troubleshoot solutions for new advanced technology systems, iterating and providing feedback to internal and external partners with each opportunity.
As an Amazonian you are able guide the development, implementation and delivery of complex system designs and advanced technology in ambiguous and complex problem spaces. You integrate systems for safety, security, stability, and efficiency. You participate in the full system development life cycle, working within broadly defined parameters, including test plan execution and solution quality needs.
You must be responsive, flexible, and able to succeed within an open collaborative environment. Amazon’s culture encourages innovation and expects engineers to take a high-level of ownership in solving complex problems.
Come help us make history!
Key job responsibilities
Work with internal and external engineering teams to successfully deliver cross-functional deployments that are high-quality — on time, on budget, maintainable, and low-defect across multiple programs.
Contribute to project priorities, establish milestones, and drive deployment schedules to meet deadlines; capture and present KPI metrics to evaluate project success and identify areas for improvement.
Deep dive technical solutions encompassing sorter system configuration, material handling integration, controller commissioning, and connectivity validation between warehouse control systems and facility equipment.
Develop and maintain scripts, automation tools, and deployment utilities that improve engineering efficiency, reduce manual effort, and enable consistent execution at scale.
Author and contribute to internal tooling and configuration code, applying software development best practices to support deployment workflows and system integrations.
Participate in design reviews and support execution efforts between internal teams and outside vendors, including equipment specifications, material flow, process design, and site layout validation.
Communicate project status effectively, answer project questions in detail, and regularly produce clear and concise summaries for the projects you own to your program management team.
Capture and synthesize the Voice of Customer (VoC) for all new product introductions and leverage this information to prioritize system defects and influence triage efforts with Product Development teams, applying lessons learned to enable acceleration and deployment scale.
Build strong working relationships with Fulfillment Center and Sort Center management and their operations teams across multiple sites, as well as Facilities, Finance, Safety, Process Engineering, and other business stakeholders.
Develop and maintain deployment standards, SOPs, and runbooks that enable consistent execution across distributed engineering teams at scale.
Identify process improvement initiatives in support of operations, deployment, or engineering teams within a geographic node.
Develop cross-functional knowledge of Operations and Engineering team systems, processes, procedures, and tools.
Collaborate with internal teams and external vendors to generate high-quality, cost-effective solutions with quick turnaround.
Travel up to 75% throughout North America, which can vary based on peak seasons.
A day in the life
Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:
Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
Maternity and Parental Leave Options
Paid Time Off (PTO)
401(k) Plan

Basic Qualifications
Experience in automating, deploying, and supporting large-scale infrastructure
Experience programming with at least one modern language such as Python, Ruby, Golang, Java, C++, C#, Rust
Experience with CI/CD pipelines build processes
Experience with Linux/Unix
Bachelor's degree
3+ years control system experience including PLC/IPC based controls design, development, implementation and support. E.g. Allen Bradley, Siemens and CODESYS systems
Experience with the designs of complex, automated material handling equipment, packaging

We are building exciting new capabilities in the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Agentic AI Automated Reasoning group by using Automated Reasoning in new, novel and exciting ways to enhance AWS services. The position is based in Seattle, Washington.
We are seeking a talented and passionate Software Development Engineer (SDE) who wishes to work at the intersection of Automated Reasoning and cloud-scale distributed systems, building and operating managed reasoning infrastructure that powers correctness guarantees across AWS.
As an SDE on the ATR team, you will design, build, and operate components of Amazon's cloud-hosted automated reasoning platform that enables AWS services to offload satisfiability and verification queries at scale. You will tackle challenges in distributed systems, solver integration, API development, and service reliability. Your work will directly enable customers to verify correctness of software, infrastructure configurations, and AI-generated code at AWS scale.
This is a unique opportunity to combine strong software engineering skills with automated reasoning technology. You'll work alongside world-class scientists and senior engineers to turn research breakthroughs in solver technology into production services that power correctness guarantees for millions of customers. The problems are hard, the impact is enormous, and your contributions will be highly visible.

Design and implement features and components of Amazon's cloud-hosted automated reasoning platform, including query routing, solver orchestration, result caching, and soundness management.
Build and maintain distributed systems that meet AWS's operational excellence standards for availability, latency, and correctness.

Job Description
As an Associate Data Scientist, you will assist the Data Scientist and other business analysts with working with business users to fully understand their needs for data science solutions. Skilled and experienced in analyzing data and have a broad understanding of core statistical and ML algorithms like multi-class classification, decision trees, support vector machine, random-forest, Gradient Boosting.
Effective communication and story-telling skills to provide insights to business units.
Energy and enthusiasm. Passion for learning and contributing to development.

description_preview:
About the Role
We are excited to offer a Fall 2026 internship opportunity designed for college students in the La Jolla, San Diego area who are able to commute to our office. As a Data Science / Software Engineer Intern, you’ll be handling real operational problems and the latitude to figure out how technology can solve them – prototyping ideas, testing what works, and helping push forward projects that genuinely change how the company runs. We run a modern stack (CINC, a custom Supabase data platform, HubSpot, RingCentral, n8n, and Google Workspace) and we use software, AI, and automation to do more with a lean team.
We’re building toward bigger things: AI systems that handle multi-step work end-to-end, internal tools that replace software we currently pay for, a continuously running engine that sources and scores acquisition targets, and live dashboards that leadership actually makes decisions from. You’ll contribute to that vision, and the more you bring curiosity and original thinking, the more you’ll get to own. This is an unpaid internship offered for academic credit. You'll gain hands-on experience with a real production stack, direct mentorship, and projects you can point to long after the internship ends.
What You'll Do
Build and test n8n automation workflows that connect our tools and eliminate repetitive manual work.
Prototype and test new ideas: take a process that’s slow or manual, propose a better way, and build a working version to see if it holds up.
Help develop AI-powered workflows using the Claude and Gemini APIs, from simple drafting and extraction toward more ambitious multi-step systems that read inputs, make decisions, and produce finished work for human review.
Run recurring data-extraction jobs, such as pulling figures from HOA financial-statement PDFs into structured spreadsheets.
Support data cleanup, entry, and validation in our Supabase platform and across spreadsheets.
Help design, build, and test internal tools and dashboards that staff use day to day: including early versions of tools that could replace software we currently buy.
Maintain data quality in HubSpot, and support the competitive-intelligence and acquisition research process by gathering, organizing, scoring, and verifying company and contact data.
Document how workflows and tools function, and take ownership of well-defined projects from start to finish.
What We're Looking For
Outside-the-box thinking. You don’t just complete the task in front of you. Ask whether there’s a smarter way to do it, and you’re eager to test your ideas rather than wait for permission.
Self-direction. Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work independently in an unstructured, fast-paced environment with minimal hands-on oversight.
Comfort with technology. You’re not intimidated by new software, spreadsheets, or learning a tool on the fly. Exposure to any of SQL, Python, automation platforms, or AI tools is a plus, but resourcefulness and a willingness to learn matter more than a finished skill set.
Analytical aptitude. Strong analytical skills and an aptitude for breaking down data and business problems.
Communication. Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with diverse team members and explain what you built and why.
Genuine interest. Real curiosity for technology, automation, and AI, and how they can transform how a business operates.
Benefits
Gain hands-on experience with a real production stack – automation (n8n), databases (Supabase/Postgres), CRMs (HubSpot), and applied AI – skills that transfer to almost any modern company.
Work on genuinely ambitious problems, not busywork, with room to propose and test your own ideas.
Work closely with experienced professionals in a collaborative, mentorship-oriented environment.
Access valuable networking opportunities within the technology and business community.
Flexible work arrangements to accommodate academic commitments.
Real projects you can point to, plus exposure to many aspects of how a growing business runs on technology.
Potential for future career growth within the organization based on performance and alignment.
To Apply
Please submit via LinkedIn and send a resume and cover letter to david@alliedlegacypartners.com, directly to the founder. Use the following subject line:
ALP Tech Intern Candidate: {Full Name}, {School}
In the cover letter, please briefly explain:
Your interest in this internship and how it fits with your current career goals.
Any relevant experience you have (coursework, work experience, projects, or things you’ve built on your own).
A time you came up with a creative or unconventional solution to a problem, or built something that didn’t exist yet.
Your ability or experience working in unstructured and ambiguous environments with minimal hands-on oversight (your ability to self-motivate and self-supervise).
Your available time commitment in person at our La Jolla, San Diego office: 20 hours per week during the school year, starting September 2026 and onward.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
Please note that all applications will be reviewed by the founder and are not automated.

THE ROLE
We are looking for a Front-End Engineer II who wants to work at the intersection of AI interaction design and enterprise-scale software. You will own the design and delivery of interfaces ranging from conversational AI configuration flows to data-rich dashboards and policy management UIs.

Agentic and conversational UX: chat-based interfaces where administrators express intent in natural language and the system translates it into precise configurations
Hybrid interaction models: seamlessly blending conversational AI with structured UI controls, knowing when chat is the right modality vs. a visual editor

Serve as Matrix's Software Solutions Developer
Support continuous process improvement and business process reengineering projects through process mapping; data collection, analysis, & visualization; and development of digital solutions
Support proposal development by providing content for the approach, schedule, or other sections as assigned in accordance with the request for proposal or request for qualifications

Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineer

Monitor the performance and reliability of deployed automations, escalating and resolving issues within your area of ownership.

As an

, you'll own the metrics, reporting and reconciliation our financial decisions rest on, turning subscription and transaction data across OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall and Custody Navigator into numbers the business can defend. As that foundation becomes automatic, the work shifts toward forecasting and modeling.
You won't start from scratch. Our dbt project is live on Databricks with a star-schema finance mart in production and documented in Unity Catalog. What's missing is the layer on top, and that layer is yours. We also run an internal AI agent that answers business questions in Slack off the semantic layer, so every metric you define and test becomes a question Finance can ask directly rather than queue.
Department Data Engineering Employment Type Permanent - Full Time Location Chicago - Remote Workplace type Fully remote Compensation $100,000 - $130,000 / year
What You'll Accomplish:
Governed metrics. Add the definitions the finance mart doesn't have yet (ARR, renewal rate, churn, CAC), versioned in dbt and documented in Unity Catalog, with the tests that make each one defensible, and wired into the agent so Finance can ask them directly.
Reporting Finance can run without you. Move the recurring finance pack into marimo, retire the Tableau views behind it, and turn a monthly hand-build into something that runs on a schedule.
Numbers that reconcile. Reconcile transactions across the app stores, payment processors, subscription systems and the ledger, with automated checks that alert rather than surface at close. Route discrepancies upstream with the evidence attached and turn each one into a test. You build the checks and escalate. Accounting owns the treatment.
Forecasting for Finance. Cohort subscriber and revenue projection, and aggregate renewal and retention forecasting, feeding the CFO's forecast and board reporting. LTV by acquisition source, feeding paid spend allocation with Growth. Pricing and promo impact, modeled before we ship rather than measured after. Individual churn propensity and uplift follow once there's a retention motion ready to act on the scores.
Models ship as scored tables in dbt and Unity Catalog, with tests, lineage and a definition the agent can answer from. Not as notebooks.
Who You Are:
Statistically rigorous. You know why a cohort curve is the wrong shape, what a model is leaking, and when a result is noise.
Fluent in finance, and unwilling to let a number you can't explain go out the door. When two systems disagree, you find out why and tell the people upstream.
An engineer who owns the number end to end, from a CFO's question through the model, the test, the report and the conversation that follows. A spreadsheet nobody can reproduce reads to you as a liability.
AI-proficient in practice, not in theory. Claude Code, coding agents and agent SDKs are part of our daily loop, and we expect you to already work this way. A lot of what used to be a week of modeling work is now an afternoon, and we're hiring for people who have internalized that.
Willing to wear several hats. This is a small team supporting four brands. Some weeks you're deep in a retention model, some weeks you're chasing an app store discrepancy or unblocking someone else's dashboard. The scope above is the center of the role, not a fence around it.
Motivated by work that matters. Families rely on these products during real moments in their lives.

3+ years in analytics engineering, data science, BI engineering or advanced analytics.
Statistical modeling shipped into a business process: forecasting, survival or cohort analysis, or propensity.

Subscription metrics you've built and defended to a finance stakeholder: ARR/MRR, renewal, churn, LTV/CAC, or cohort revenue.
Strong SQL and real dimensional modeling. You've designed marts, not just queried them.
Python and Git as daily habits.
Nice To Have, Not a Dealbreaker:
dbt, Databricks and Unity Catalog, or a comparable lakehouse.
Reconciling transactional data to a financial system of record.
Code-first notebook reporting (marimo, Hex, Streamlit, Quarto).

Product Engineer
Harmony, New York City. Hybrid: one to two days a week in our Manhattan office. Full-time. $130,000 to $180,000 base plus equity.
Millions of Americans qualify for support they never receive, because the system asks the most of the people with the least room to spare. Harmony is reimagining how people access essential services, starting with affordable housing in New York City. Housing is the entry point; access to every benefit a family already qualifies for is the destination.
The role
We're hiring a Product Engineer to own the day-to-day of our products: what's broken, what customers need next, what we build, and whether it works. You'll do that across our existing and future product portfolio, working hand-in-hand with our CEO, our engineers, and our designer. You'll also play a pivotal role in shaping the future of Harmony's products: which problems we take on next, what we build for them, and how we get there.
It's a product job for someone who works the way we work. Nearly everything at Harmony runs through Claude or another agentic tool, and this role is no exception: when you have an idea, you'll build it before you write about it. You don't need a traditional engineering background. You do need to be a product person who can stand up their own test environment, prototype an idea, build a skill the team needs, and produce a wireframe on our design system.
What you'll do
Sit with the marketing agents and compliance managers using Harmony, watch them work a real batch of applicants, and come back knowing what to build next
Figure out what Harmony looks like for future opportunities (SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, etc.): the rules, the people who run them, and the families applying
Use the product the way an agent and an applicant do, and catch what's wrong: bugs, rough edges, and places where it doesn't match how the regulations actually work
Turn an idea into a working prototype, and put it in front of the team or a customer the same week
Write the PRDs and tickets that engineers and agents build from, whether the source is a customer request, a bug you found, or a product we haven't started yet
Be the person our customers reach first: answer them, reproduce what they hit, and make the materials that keep them from hitting it again
Run our standups, clear blockers, and build the tools and processes a small agentic team needs
Pick up whatever else the team needs. We're at a stage where everyone is close to every part of the work
What we're looking for
You ship.
You have an active GitHub with projects you built and contributions you made, and you got there with Claude Code, Cursor, or similar. You don't need to be an engineer in the traditional sense, but you do need to be able to take an idea to working software with agentic tools.
You've owned product decisions.
We don't require a particular title or path. We care that you've decided what to build, why, and in what order, with actual customers on the other end, and that you got there by doing your own research: talking to the people involved, synthesizing what you heard, and changing your mind because of it.
You take initiative.
When you want to know whether something works, you go find out. When something new comes up, whether that's our design system, a housing regulation, or a tool you've never used, you dig in rather than wait. There's a whole team here to help, but we're looking for people who start on their own.
You communicate well.
In writing and in person, with engineers, customers, and founders alike. On a small, distributed team, effective communication is vital.
Bonus points
Experience working in or around housing, public benefits, civic tech, real estate, or another highly regulated industry
You've worked at an early-stage startup before
Computer science or engineering background
Experience shipping products or features built on an LLM
You don't need to check every box. If most of this describes you, apply.
Why Harmony
Every year, millions of people qualify for things they're entitled to (housing, health coverage, food support) and never receive them, not because they're ineligible but because getting there is harder than it should be.
We're not here to make an old process a little faster. We're here to rebuild how people get access to what they're entitled to.
We're early, and we're moving fast. You'll join a small team at the ground floor and help lay out the phases of a mission that begins with housing in New York and runs through every essential service in the country. That's a large circle of people to invite in: the families applying, the agents serving them, the developers and agencies behind the buildings, and eventually the government itself. The chance to build something this significant, this early, comes along about once in a career. This is one of them.
Pay and equity
$130,000 to $180,000 base depending on experience, plus meaningful early-stage equity. Unlimited PTO and a flexible remote-working policy. You must be authorized to work in the US; we're not able to sponsor visas at this time.
How to apply
Email careers@harmonyworks.com with the subject "Product Engineer: your name" and three things: your resume, a link to your GitHub with projects you actually built, and a short note in your own words (two or three paragraphs) on why this role, where you're strongest, and what you want to get better at. We read every one.
Harmony is an equal opportunity employer.
